title: Implicit Causality-biases in humans and LLMs as a tool for benchmarking LLM discourse capabilities

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting mono- and multilingual language models with sentence fragments containing Implicit Causality verbs and specific connectives (e.g., 'because', 'and so', or a comma), generating full sentence continuations, and semi-automatically annotating the outputs to measure coreference preferences, coherence relation generation, and the anaphoric forms (e.g., pronouns vs. proper names) used.

Manipulating the gender order of the antecedents (e.g., female subject-male object vs. male subject-female object) in the sentence completion prompts and analyzing whether the gender of the referents significantly affects the models' coreference resolution behavior using mixed-effects regression models.
